title: Resurrection of the Dead
english: Human beings were created for a life of incorruptibility, and also for resurrection, as God does not resurrect for punishment, but rather an act of his compassion.

You may agree with this statement, and if so, I will refrain from inquiring about the manner in which the dead are raised and the nature of the body they will have, specifically whether the body that comes from the earth, which is subject to decay, will be revived, or if it will be a different body altogether, yet still derived from the original.
I believe that the correct understanding of faith leads us to this very flesh, the resurrection, for Christ, as the firstborn from the dead, is the resurrection of those who have fallen asleep.

Since this doctrine may not be pleasing to everyone, let us set aside the arguments that others consider valid and instead focus on what is likely, considering how God shows his concern for human creation, as seen in the book of Job, where God says, 'If you took earth's clay and formed a living being, and put it on the earth to speak?' (Job 4:19)

This is a remarkable statement, as it is beyond all wonder to create a rational living being from earth, and after creating humanity and forming them from the earth, God blessed them, saying, 'Increase and multiply, and fill the earth' (Genesis 1:28).

The apostle Paul uses an excellent example, employing a fine paradigm, when he says that the body is like a seed that is sown in the earth, but it will be raised in a different form, clothed and covered with the qualities that have been grown within it, like a reed and its leaves, as I speak of a reed and its leaf.

God gives to each of the seeds its own body, for not all who have fallen asleep will be raised in glory, even if all are in incorruption, for it is not fitting for the unseemly and the workers of evil to be crowned with glory from God.

The resurrection of the dead is a complex topic, and God distributes to the seeds, which differ, a body to each in the manner He chooses, as He says, 'What you sow is not the body that will be' (1 Corinthians 15:37), and there are heavenly and earthly bodies.

The word is one, but divided into different kinds, and all bodies will be raised in incorruption, but there will be a difference in glory and the clothing which God gives to each according to their worth, with the glory of the heavenly being different from the glory of the earthly.

This difference is demonstrated by two examples, the grain of wheat and the heavenly bodies, and it is said that what is sown in corruption is raised in incorruption, as the grain of wheat, when sown in the earth, is naked and dead, but is raised in a covering of body and an addition of…
